jobs.occupation: Software Director - Industrial Automation, Robotics and Integrated AI
jobs.description:

• Experience with software that enables physical products; industrial automation is strongly preferred.

Our leadership culture is built on trust, constructive conflict, commitment, peer accountability, and collective results. Location and Working Model 

The role is based at Inwatec’s office in Odense, Denmark. Our standard working model is office-based. English is the corporate language; much of the everyday office conversation is in Danish, so Danish capability is preferred.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a 3-year PhD stipend in the field of quantum control theory for quantum algorithms within the general study programme Electronical and Electronic Engineering, as per January 1st 2027, or soon hereafter.

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Your work tasks

The position is part of the research project QUANTA – Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. Real quantum computers are open quantum systems: noise and decoherence act on the computation while it runs, so the idealised picture of a sequence of perfect unitary gates acting on an isolated system does not hold in practice. QUANTA therefore regards a quantum program as an open dynamical system, described by Kraus operators in discrete time and by the controlled Lindblad master equation in continuous time, and treats the choice of quantum gates as control decisions. The aim is to use control theory to design quantum algorithms, in particular optimisation algorithms, that are robust to noise and disturbances.

As a PhD student you will work mainly on two parts of the project. The first concerns reach-avoidance for quantum systems: computing the probability that a quantum process reaches a target set of states before it enters a set of forbidden states, and designing control strategies, for example by dynamic programming, that steer the computation towards its goal while respecting such constraints. You will develop this theory for quantum Markov chains described by Kraus operators and for continuous-time systems described by the Lindblad master equation.

The second part applies these results to quantum optimisation. You will develop algorithms in which an optimisation problem, starting with semidefinite programming and continuing with bilinear and polynomial problems, is solved by a quantum system regarded as a control system, including constrained problems formulated as reach-avoidance. You will analyse how the resulting quantum circuits scale with the problem size and test the algorithms on a real quantum computer.

You will work closely with the principal investigator, a postdoctoral researcher on the project and the project's international collaborators, and the project includes research stays at partner institutions abroad. You will present your results at international conferences and in scientific journals, and they will form the basis of your PhD thesis. As part of the PhD programme you will follow PhD courses and take part in teaching and supervision of student projects at the department.

Your competencies You hold a Master's degree in control engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with a solid mathematical background, for example in linear algebra, dynamical systems, control theory, optimisation or probability theory, and with a genuine interest in quantum computing.

Knowledge of quantum mechanics or quantum information is an advantage, but not a requirement – what matters is that you are motivated to learn it during the project. Programming experience, for example in Python, is also an advantage. We value curiosity, the ability to work independently and the willingness to share ideas and help colleagues. You communicate well in English, both orally and in writing.

Qualification requirements

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

The position is hosted by the Learning and Decisions Lab at the Department of Electronic Systems, Aalborg University, led by Professor Rafal Wisniewski. The lab develops theory and algorithms at the intersection of control theory, stochastic systems, optimisation and quantum computing, including stability and safety of stochastic and quantum systems and feedback control of quantum hardware. You will join a team of senior researchers, PhD students and postdoctoral fellows working on related problems, in an informal and international environment with weekly meetings and close day-to-day supervision

How to apply

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

The work will focus on electrolysers, fuel-synthesis processes, energy storage, heat integration, and interactions with the electrical grid.

You will combine process simulation with operational optimization, process control, techno-economic assessment, and model validation to investigate flexible operation under varying renewable electricity generation and energy prices.

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient retention in agricultural waters
jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies.

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling

• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data

• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures

• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals

Your profile

The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands

• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python

• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals

We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The successful candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management. The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department aims to be a supportive and encouraging workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer

The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information

For further information, please contact Senior Researcher Joachim Audet, joau@ecos.au.dk.

Deadline

Application procedure

This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies. 

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling
• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data
• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures
• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals
Your profile
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands
• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python
• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals
We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. jobs.description:
We offer PhD scholarships at DTU Compute to develop machine learning methods for faster analysis and optimization of cyber-physical systems. You will build predictive models of expensive analytical calculations and simulations, and use AI to find good solutions to optimization problems that cannot be solved exactly within practical computing budgets. 

You will join the Embedded Systems Engineering section and work with Prof. Paul Pop. The application areas are related to, e.g., software-defined vehicles, datacenters, industrial automation, and energy systems.

Your research will connect learned prediction models with optimization methods. The PhD topics will be defined with the supervisors. You will:

• Develop surrogate models that predict results of complex analyses and simulations, such as execution delays, energy use, and resource demands.
• Use machine learning to guide configuration, scheduling, and resource allocation, reducing the need for expensive model evaluations.
• Evaluate solution quality, computing time, uncertainty, and transfer to new systems; check proposed solutions against the original models and constraints.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Computational Genomics
jobs.description:
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is offering a postdoctoral position in computational genomics, starting 01-02-2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position will be available for a 2,5-year period.

You will be part of a research environment focusing on computational genomics, bioinformatics, and AI-driven plant research. You will be contributing specifically to the area of development of computational methods that integrate pangenomic information and large language model (LLM)-based approaches and the focus of your position will be targeted long-read sequencing and high-resolution gene-space assembly in complex plant genomes. You will work experimentally with genomic datasets, develop and evaluate LLM-based methods, and validate sequencing workflows and gene-space assembly quality.

We expect that you will be an important part of the research environment and that you will contribute positively to the social working environment. We also expect that you will take part in our teaching activities and that you will report research results in high-impact scientific journals.

Your profile

We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has

• A PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a closely related discipline, with a deep focus on plant genomics, computational plant biology, or AI applications in plant science .

• Documented experience in computational genomics, bioinformatics, pangenomic data analysis, machine learning, deep learning, or LLM-based model development.

• Collaborative skills and ability to contribute effectively in teams. A fondness of taking the initiative and the motivation to pursue a scientific career.

Additional qualifications

Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

• Experience with Oxford Nanopore sequencing or other long-read sequencing platforms.

• Experience in LLM-based model development, including model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation.

• Experience developing computational methods or software for genomic sequence analysis.

• Experience with high-performance computing, algorithm optimization, or large-scale genomic datasets

• Familiarity with pangenomic analysis, structural variation, or genome assembly

• Teaching and supervision experience at the BSc and MSc level

• Interest and experience in developing effective national and international research applications

At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. • An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.

Living and working in Denmark

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position on statistical genetics in plant breeding with special focus on cultivar mixtures in wheat
jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position

The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The position provides excellent possibilities for access to state-of-the-art tools for simulation and for the analysis of complex genomic datasets, writing publications, and collaboration with industry partners as well as with other national and international research groups.

Qualifications

• 
Ph.D. or equivalent in plant/animal breeding, quantitative genetics, quantitative genomics, statistics, or related fields.

• 
Strong interest in use of stochastic models for the analysis of phenotypic and genomic data.

• 
Dedicated to developed statistical models in modern plant breeding

• 
Good understanding of methods used in genomic prediction.

• 
General understanding of commercial breeding programs.

• 
Inspiration and experience from working in a commercial breeding program will be valuable.

• 
Good ability to conduct large-scale computations.

• 
Documented skills in writing and publishing papers of the highest international standard.

• 
Good skills in oral and written communication in English.

•

Who we are:

Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG)

The institute like center, QGG, is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and quantitative genomics () at Aarhus University. We perform basic and applied research within livestock and plant breeding as well as human applications in precision medicine. The research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development, basic analysis, and application of the developed methods on practical problems across species in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research Center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strive for an excellent working environment. We therefore value self-leadership, open communication, respect for diversity and success in mentoring, supervision and teaching. The main work location will be the main campus close to Aarhus city center.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.
